answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and isolated to the primary region during settlement peak. Rollback is unavailable because the in-flight security patch must not be reverted. Circuit breaking would drop customer writes, and read-replica routing addresses reporting load rather than the write path. Capacity headroom was historically provisioned before a peak, not proven as a mid-incident fix for a region-scoped, post-release write regression. memory_b2 is the closest precedent (regional failover restored latency within minutes) but is a single archived case, so cut over as a standard experiment rather than an immediate broad shift, and treat secondary-region headroom, replication/settlement effects, and whether the patch is what is actually hurting writes as still uncertain.
